_comment: North America stage: which power holds each downloaded polygon. Authored attributes only; no geometry. Categories are the legend's fill keys (Set A tokens) or patterns. OpenHistoricalMap country- and colony-level polygons (admin level 2, and aboriginal lands) take the first rule whose pattern matches their English or local name inside the rule's dates; provinces (levels 3 and 4) take the power of the level-2 polygon that contains them at each date, and fall back to the rules. A name no rule names is 'other': drawn muted, with its border and its name, never guessed. Newberry polygons are 'us', except TERR_TYPE 'Other' (Vermont Republic, Oregon Country, Uncertain Boundary Area, Republic of Texas, Deseret), which is 'disputed'. Dates are YYYYMMDD.

nolabel._why: OpenHistoricalMap keeps this name on Spain's Caribbean remainder until 1899; the viceroyalty ended with Mexican independence. The Captaincy General's own name is shown instead.

native_exclude._why: historical-basemaps' 1492 map takes its North American homelands from Native Land Digital, which maps present-day territories; the Métis nation formed in the 1700s and cannot stand on a 1492 or 1530 map.

_claims: Lesson maps (src/us/frames.js) name a hatch by its sides: 'Claimed by Texas and Mexico'. A computed overlap knows its two polygons; an area that OpenHistoricalMap or Newberry draws whole as disputed takes its sides from the first rule here whose pattern matches its name. Authored attributes, each with its reason; owner to review (docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-06). A disputed area no rule names keeps the general label.

claims._why: Newberry's own record: 'Texas declared its independence from Mexico' (New Handbook of Texas, 5:537-538). Mexico did not recognize that independence before annexation; its claim ended with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848), which fixed the Rio Grande line.
OpenHistoricalMap's own name for the land both claimed, 2 March 1836 – 28 December 1845 (relation 2693046).
Newberry's own record: 'The boundary from Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mtns. between the United States and the British possessions was unsettled' (to the Convention of 1818).

Newberry's records: the United States claimed the Oregon Country from 1804, and 'The Oregon Boundary Treaty between the United States and Great Britain ended joint occupancy of the Oregon Country' (its record of 15 June 1846).

Newberry's own record: 'Vermont declared its independence from New York in 1777. Although not recognized as a separate state by the Continental Congress, Vermont functioned as an independent republic until statehood in 1791.'
